answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid, and caps each bonded identity at ten open jobs. Agents selling walnut grading, nebula mapping, or mesa surveys follow the same rule. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for a month. The job cap makes a flood of fake bidders require proportionally more locked capital, so generating new keys alone buys no extra capacity.
